chapter: Willie Lynch, the Blue Rhythm Band and Teddy Hill
title: Lynch band at the Lafayette Theatre and Irving Mills
summary: After the Savoy closed the band scattered, then Lynch's group had a hit playing 'Stardust' at the Lafayette Theatre and Irving Mills put them in the Cotton Club.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it

blocks.x: You mentioned that this band, you left it and then went into the Apollo.
Well, that was later, after we came out of

the Savoy... Well, you know, when you close down a job and you don't have anywhere to go, it looks like every man goes for himself, and try to find some work with whoever he can. So we finished the Savoy, and we didn't have nowhere to go; well, everybody started looking for what they can get.
Because what I understood was that Willie Lynch made a hit at the Apollo, and that's when Irving Mills...
And that's when Irving Mills asked him to come in and form the Mills Blue Rhythm Band.

Yeah, that was a little later. That's after we'd come out of the Savoy, and I had got away from the band. I don't know if I was with Luis Russell or who I was with. I know I wasn't still with Willie Lynch. Because when they went in the Apollo, Willie was out all up and down the street, how great this band was in the Apollo playing "Stardust." "Stardust" wasn't even heard of. I guess it was still on the shelf, in the publisher's office somewhere. So I heard about the band, you know, from the street. And they were doing record-breaking business in the theatre, in the Lafayette Theatre.
Soon after that, when they finished the year/gig(?), Irving Mills put them in the Cotton Club to take...
So it was the Lafayette Theatre, not the Apollo, then.
The Lafayette Theatre. That's where "Stardust"... And that's where all these stars were coming down...
That's where the stars were coming down from the theatre(?)...
